text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Friday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- Prime Minister Andris Shkele gave more details of the sacking of Defence Minister Andrejs Krastinsh and state defence secretary Einar Vaivods. He said Vaivods broke the rules in many ways and increased the price of the fuel to be bought.
- A bill on the status of asylum-seekers passed its first reading in parliament.
- There were several events to mark the anniversary of the the end of World War Two.
- Parliament voted to extend the range of people allowed to buy land in urban areas.
- Local government officials may have broken anti-corruption laws by combining their job with work on the councils of ports, for which they are paid.
- The World Bank has lent $18 million for pension reform
- A verdict of the constitutional court means that energy prices will rise by 40 percent to 2000.
- The head of parliament's foreign affairs committee is positive on the visit of Russian MPs.
- Latvia will celebrate the Day of Europe for the first time today
- The privatisation agency accepted the restructure programme for the Dautek textiles firm in the eastern town of Daugavpils which is aimed at preventing its bankruptcy.
